subject: Maths
title: Ordering positive and negative integers
subtitle: Place Value and Ordering Integers · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can order and compare positive and negative integers using a number line.

key_vocab.definition: Integers are whole numbers including negatives, zero, and positives. On a number line, numbers increase from left to right.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can order and compare positive and negative integers using a number line.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Ordering integers -- Integers are whole numbers including negatives, zero, and positives. On a number line, numbers increase from left to right.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Picture a number line: numbers to the right are always bigger. Negative numbers are to the left of zero.
-8 -3 0 < 4 < 9
Left = smaller, Right = bigger

Key examples:
  ✓ -5 < -2 < 0 < 3 < 7  (ordered smallest to largest)
  ✓ -10 is less than -3  (further from zero = smaller)
  ✓ 0 is greater than any negative number  (zero is not negative)
  ✗ -5 > -2 because 5 > 2  (ignore the sign is wrong)
  ✗ -3 is greater than 0  (all negatives are less than 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – ordering negatives
  Put these in order from smallest to largest: -3, 5, -7, 2, -1
  Most negative = smallest: -7
  Then -3, -1, 2, 5
  -7, -3, -1, 2, 5
  -7, -3, -1, 2, 5
  (The more negative a number, the smaller it is.)

Example 2 – comparing two integers
  Which is greater: -4 or -9?
  -4 is closer to zero than -9
  On the number line, -4 is to the right of -9
  -4 > -9
  -4 is greater
  (Closer to zero means bigger for negative numbers.)

sections.title: Real-world contexts
sections.content:
Order from smallest to largest.

(a) Temperatures: -3°C, 7°C, -12°C, 0°C, 4°C
(b) Bank balance: -£50, £20, -£15, £0, -£80
(c) Sea level (m): -40, 120, -120, 5, -5
(d) Floor levels: -2, 3, -1, 0, 5

sections.title: Mixed ordering
sections.content:
Answer each question.

(a) Which is smaller: -99 or -100?
(b) Order: 4, -4, 40, -40, 0
(c) Find a number between -5 and -3
(d) How many integers between -3 and 3 (not including -3 and 3)?
(e) Order: -2.5, -3, 1, -1.5, 0.5

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ -5 is less than -2
✗ -5 > -2 because 5 > 2
✓ 0 is greater than any negative number
✗ -100 is greater than -1
✓ On a number line, right means bigger
